hero.headline: Indian River Sheriff says two deaths near Sebastian River Bridge not connected
hero.teaser: Two bodies found within two days near the Sebastian River bridge are not connected, according to the Indian River County Sheriff.
hero.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office says there is no connection between two deaths that occurred near the Sebastian River bridge within a two-day period, though both remain under investigation as suspicious.

Authorities discovered two bodies in the area near the Sebastian River bridge over the course of two days. The sheriff's office examined both incidents to determine whether they might be related but found no evidence linking the deaths. Despite ruling out a connection between the cases, investigators continue to treat both deaths as suspicious while they work to determine what happened in each situation.

The bodies were found in close proximity to each other near the Sebastian River bridge, raising initial questions about whether the deaths might be connected. The brief time frame between the discoveries prompted law enforcement to carefully review both cases for any potential links. After conducting their investigation, sheriff's officials stated they have not found evidence suggesting the two deaths are related to one another.

Both investigations remain active as authorities work to gather more information about each case. The sheriff's office has not released additional details about the circumstances surrounding either death or the identities of the individuals found near the bridge. Investigators continue working to piece together what led to each death in the Sebastian area.

cards.headline: New Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as grocery costs continue to rise
cards.teaser: A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, offering Martin County shoppers an affordable option as food prices contin.
cards.body:
A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to Martin County customers. Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited to have an affordable option close to their home. Cheryl Cooperman said she is thrilled to have a store with reasonable prices nearby and that grocery prices are getting expensive and changing the way she shops. She said they never used to look at prices, but now she will go with what is on sale instead of just what they want.

The opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1%. Egg prices are dropping, and beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1% from April to May, and chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period. Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday that prices are going to stay inflated and are not going to go down. They said having stores like Aldi for the average person is extremely beneficial because there is nobody who is not feeling the price increase.

The St. Lucie Mets committed five errors and gave up 17 hits in a 15-3 loss to the Jupiter Hammerheads on Camp Day at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium on Thursday afternoon.

Jupiter scored in each of its final seven innings at the plate, steadily pulling away after the Mets grabbed an early lead.

Antonio Jimenez put St. Lucie ahead 2-1 with a two-run homer in the third inning, his second home run in the last three games and his fifth of the season with the Mets. The lead did not last. Jupiter answered with four runs in the bottom of the third to go up 5-2, keyed by a two-run single from Max Williams and an RBI double from Nixon Chirinos.

Jackson Hauge trimmed the deficit to 5-3 with a two-out RBI single in the fourth, but that was the last Mets hit until Elian Peña singled with one out in the eighth. In between, Jupiter reliever Elier Morillo retired all 10 batters he faced, striking out seven.

The Hammerheads kept adding on, scoring two in the fourth, two in the fifth and four in the sixth, the last punctuated by a three-run homer from Chirinos off Caden Wooster.

All nine Jupiter starters reached base and eight collected hits. Leadoff man Luis Cova went 4 for 5, a triple shy of the cycle, while Williams finished 2 for 5 with a homer, three RBI and three runs. For St. Lucie, Peña, Branny De Oleo and Francisco Toledo each went 2 for 4.

Mets starter Christian Rodriguez took the loss, charged with five runs on eight hits over three innings. He did not walk a batter and struck out five.

The Mets (4-12, 37-45) and Hammerheads (7-11, 44-40) continue their series Friday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium, with first pitch set for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie ranked 67th most stressed city in United States
cards.teaser: A WalletHub study compared 182 cities across 39 metrics including work hours, unemployment, divorce and suicide rates. Port St. Lucie was cited as the 42nd most financially stressed city in America.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie was ranked the 67th most stressed city in the United States according to a study released this month by WalletHub. The study compared 182 cities across 39 metrics including average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates. The report cited Port St. Lucie as the 42nd most financially stressed city in America.

Jacksonville is the most stressed city in Florida, topping out at number 37 in the United States. Compared to other states, Florida performed fairly well, with no cities in the top 35 most stressed. In South Florida, Miami was on the list at number 50 with affordable housing being fourth worst in the country, and Fort Lauderdale at number 83.

WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo said cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. "Some stress is out of our control, due to issues with family, friends or employers. However, where you live can play a big role in how stressed you are," Lupo said. "When moving, it's important to consider how a certain city may impact your mental health – not just your financial opportunities." The report found that money, health and the economy all remain top stressors.

Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana topped the list of most stressed cities in the United States. Fremont, California in the Bay Area topped the list of least stressed cities, followed by South Burlington, Vermont, and Bismarck and Fargo, North Dakota. Fremont is a notably affluent area with average home prices of about $1.5 million.

hero.headline: Park Vista Cobras target state playoffs after strong finish to 2025 season
hero.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The Cobras struggled to find their footing early in 2025, but finished strong, winning four of their last five games.

"Felt good throughout the second half of that season," senior Harris Bender said. "We're just working towards being able to carry that through the whole season, like you said, and we have all the pieces in place now, it's just about executing." The team believes it has assembled the right roster to make a deep postseason run, though players acknowledge the work required to reach their goals. "Coming in, I feel like we got the guys that we need to get it done," senior Erik Lee said. "But also, we got to put the work in to get there as well."

The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017. Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna emphasized the importance of maintaining focus throughout the season rather than looking too far ahead. "We got to take it one game at a time," Hanna said. "We can't look past anyone. We got to handle business weekly and if we do that, do our job, that'll get us in the playoffs." The approach reflects lessons learned from their 2025 campaign, when the Cobras needed time to develop consistency before finding their rhythm late in the year.

Senior Justice Jones expressed confidence that the team will achieve its championship aspirations. "It's going to feel amazing, because I already know it's gonna happen, definitely," Jones said. Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August. The Cobras will look to avoid the slow start that plagued them last season and instead carry their late 2025 momentum into the opening weeks of the new campaign.

cards.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League unveils team names ahead of August debut
cards.teaser: The Women's Professional Baseball League released the nicknames and logos of its four teams Wednesday, with each team name inspired by pioneering women.
cards.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women. Kelsie Whitmore, the star pitcher who was the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis, the history-making former Little League sensation, will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. There is also the New York Heights and the Boston Hunters.

The WPBL's debut season begins on August 1 in Springfield, Illinois. Games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium and will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs. The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. The San Francisco Firebells were inspired by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as Firebelle, who was a champion of San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the Queen of the Diamond. The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist.

cards.headline: Karolina Muchova defeats Coco Gauff to reach Wimbledon final in dramatic tiebreaker
cards.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker.
cards.body:
The ninth-ranked Muchova defeated Gauff 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) on Thursday in a match that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker. It will be Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova is the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, champion in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, champion in 2024. Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal next on Centre Court.

For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. announced the return of the 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival to Vero Beach this November.

The festival marks nearly two decades of the annual event returning to the area. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. organizes the festival.

The event will take place in Vero Beach during November 2026. The festival has become an annual tradition for the Treasure Coast community.

Further details about specific dates, location, vendors and activities will be announced by the event organizers in the coming months.
